A double-sided patch to commemorate the Artemis 2 mission, which will carry four astronauts on a flight around the Moon. This special edition patch features the standard Artemis 2 crew emblem on one side, while the second side reverses the position of the Moon and the Earth. NASA says this patch designates the mission as “AII,” signifying not only the second major flight of the Artemis campaign, but also an endeavor of discovery that seeks to explore for all and by all. Framed in Apollo 8’s famous Earthrise photo, the scene of the Earth and the Moon represents the dual nature of human spaceflight, both equally compelling: The Moon represents our exploration destination, focused on discovery of the unknown. The Earth represents home, focused on the perspective we gain when we look back at our shared planet and learn what it is to be uniquely human. The orbit around Earth highlights the ongoing exploration missions that have enabled Artemis to set sights on a long-term presence on the Moon and soon, Mars. Measures approx. 4.5 x 4 inches. Liftoff of Artemis 2 from pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center is scheduled during a launch window that opens at 6:24 p.m. EDT (2224 UTC). NASA astronaut and mission commander Reid Wiseman leads the crew, which includes fellow NASA astronauts Victor Glover and Christina Koch along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen. The SLS rocket will take an easterly trajectory on departure from Florida's Space Coast. Our live coverage of the final countdown and launch with commentary from Spaceflight Now's Will Robinson-Smith will start soon after the completion of fueling.
